FileFormat.description: Output format of a generated lineup, taken from the `format` query parameter.
FileFormat.title: FileFormat

HealthResponse.description: Body of the health endpoint: `ok`, or `unavailable` when the database check failed.
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

InvitationCreate.description:
Body for creating an invite link. The link stops working after `expires_in_hours`
(2, 24 or 72; default 24): a short life limits the damage if it is forwarded further than
intended. Anyone who opens it while signed in joins as a member.
InvitationCreate.title: InvitationCreate

InvitationCreated.description:
A freshly created invite link. `code` and `url` are shown **only in this response**: the
server keeps just a hash, so they cannot be shown again. Send `url` to the person you want
to invite.
InvitationCreated.title: InvitationCreated

InvitationPreview.description:
What anyone holding a link may see before signing in: the team's name, the display name of
whoever created the link (if their sign-in provided one) and when the link expires. Nothing
else about the team or its members.
InvitationPreview.title: InvitationPreview

InvitationResponse.description:
An invite link that still works, as listed to the team's owners. It carries no code (that
was shown once, at creation); `id` is what you pass to revoke it.
InvitationResponse.title: InvitationResponse

LineupRequest.description:
Everything needed to fill one lineup sheet (no database involved).

Text fields are trimmed, must not be empty and have a maximum length. Only the coach is
required among the staff: `doctor`, `assistant_coach`, `team_leader` and `ball_thrower` may be
omitted or blank (the sheet prints them empty), the same as for saved lineups. `players` holds 1 to 15
entries with unique cap numbers (1-15) and unique NSSZ numbers.
LineupRequest.title: LineupRequest

MemberResponse.description:
One member of a team: id, role, join date and, when known, their name. `display_name` is
the Google name the member's own token carried the last time they used the app; it is `null`
for someone who has not opened the app since names were introduced, so show a fallback
such as "Member 2". No e-mail addresses are stored. `is_you` marks the caller's own row so a
client can show "(you)" and a Leave button.
MemberResponse.title: MemberResponse

OwnershipTransfer.description: Body for handing a team over: the member who becomes its owner.
OwnershipTransfer.title: OwnershipTransfer

PaginatedPlayers.description: One page of players plus the total number of matching players.
PaginatedPlayers.title: PaginatedPlayers

PaginatedSavedLineups.description: One page of saved lineups plus the total number of matching lineups.
PaginatedSavedLineups.title: PaginatedSavedLineups

PaginatedTeams.description: One page of teams plus the total number of teams.
PaginatedTeams.title: PaginatedTeams

PlayerCreate.description:
Body for creating a player. Text is trimmed, must not be blank or contain control
characters; `team_id` is the roster to add the player to and must be a team you belong to.
PlayerCreate.title: PlayerCreate

PlayerRequest.description: One player on the lineup sheet.
PlayerRequest.title: PlayerRequest

PlayerResponse.description: A player as returned by the API.
PlayerResponse.title: PlayerResponse

PlayerUpdate.description:
Body for replacing a player's data (all fields are overwritten, including `team_id`,
which may move the player to another team you belong to).
PlayerUpdate.title: PlayerUpdate

SavedLineupCreate.description:
Body for saving a new lineup.

`team_id` is the workspace the lineup is saved in (a team you belong to); every member of
that team can then see it. It is independent of `source_team_id`, which only says where the
team *name* comes from. The other fields and their rules are described on `SavedLineupFields`.
SavedLineupCreate.title: SavedLineupCreate

SavedLineupPlayerCreate.description:
One player slot: reference an existing roster player (whose current
name/NSSZ number is copied in when the lineup is saved or edited) or supply free text
directly, never both.
SavedLineupPlayerCreate.title: SavedLineupPlayerCreate

SavedLineupPlayerResponse.description: A player slot of a saved lineup, as copied when it was saved or last edited.
SavedLineupPlayerResponse.title: SavedLineupPlayerResponse

SavedLineupResponse.description:
A saved lineup as returned by the API. All text is the copy taken when it was saved or
last edited; `source_*_id` fields are soft references and become null if the source is
deleted. `team_id` is the workspace the lineup lives in.

`updated_at` is when it was last saved: equal to `created_at` until the first edit. Send it
back as `expected_updated_at` when you edit the lineup.
SavedLineupResponse.title: SavedLineupResponse

SavedLineupUpdate.description:
Body for editing a saved lineup in place (`PUT /lineups/saved/{id}`).

The same fields and rules as a new lineup, without `team_id`: a lineup never moves to another
team. Every field is replaced, and the player list replaces all the old player slots. A
`source_*_id` is resolved again, so a roster player picked now is copied with their current
name and NSSZ number. A slot whose roster player was deleted comes back from `GET` with
`source_player_id: null`, so send it as free text (`name` and `nssz_number`).

`expected_updated_at` is the `updated_at` of the version you loaded. If someone saved a newer
version in the meantime, the edit is refused with 409 and nothing changes: reload the lineup
and apply your change to the new version. It must carry a timezone (the API returns UTC with
one), so send back exactly the value you received.
SavedLineupUpdate.title: SavedLineupUpdate

StaffResponse.description: A staff entry as returned by the API.

source_player_id.description: The roster player it was picked from; `null` for a typed-in name or once that player was deleted.
source_player_id.title: Source Player Id

StaffResponse.title: StaffResponse

StaffRole.description:
The staff roles a team can keep. Stored as text (not a database enum), like `TeamRole`.
There is deliberately no `doctor`: that field stays a per-lineup free text.
StaffRole.title: StaffRole

StaffWrite.description:
Body for creating a staff entry or replacing one (`PUT` overwrites every field).

`name` is trimmed, must not be blank or contain control characters. It is stored as a copy:
when you pick a roster player, send their name here and their id as `source_player_id`; the
entry then keeps the name even after the player is deleted or renamed.

is_default.description: Make this the team's default for its role. The previous default of that role, if any, stops being the default in the same transaction.
is_default.title: Is Default

role.description: Which staff role this person fills.

source_player_id.description: The roster player this entry was picked from, or omitted for a typed-in name. Must be a player of this same team, otherwise 404. The name is not kept in sync with the player.
source_player_id.title: Source Player Id

StaffWrite.title: StaffWrite

TeamCreate.description:
Body for creating a team. `division` is the team's usual division (optional, at most 100
characters), which the lineup creator pre-fills; `home_venue` is its home venue (optional, at
most 200 characters), which pre-fills the location of a home lineup. The name is trimmed and
must not be blank or contain control characters.
TeamCreate.title: TeamCreate

TeamDeleteResponse.description: Confirmation returned after a team is deleted.
TeamDeleteResponse.title: TeamDeleteResponse

TeamPoolItem.description:
Entry of the shared opponent directory: `id` and `name` and nothing else, on purpose.
Listing a team must never reveal its roster, members or lineups.
TeamPoolItem.title: TeamPoolItem

TeamResponse.description:
A team as returned by the API, from the signed-in caller's point of view.

`role` is the caller's role in the team (`owner` or `member`); `created_by` is who created
it (audit only, it grants nothing). `is_public` means "listed in the opponent directory".
`division` is the team's default division (`null` when unset), used to pre-fill new lineups.
`home_venue` is the team's home venue (`null` when unset), used to pre-fill the location of a
lineup played at home.
TeamResponse.title: TeamResponse

TeamUpdate.description:
Body for updating a team (owners only). `name` is always required; `is_public` lists or
unlists the team in the opponent directory and `division` sets its default division; both are
left unchanged when omitted (so a division cannot be cleared once set, only replaced).
`home_venue` sets the team's home venue and follows the same rule.
TeamUpdate.title: TeamUpdate

HTTPBearer.description: Supabase access token (JWT) of the signed-in user.

get.description:
Liveness by default; `?db=1` adds a `SELECT 1` readiness probe.

A failing probe returns a plain 503 body instead of raising, so the driver's error
text (which can contain hostnames) never reaches the client and health checks don't
flood Sentry.

parameters.description: Also check the database (readiness). Default: liveness only.
parameters.name: db

schema.description: Also check the database (readiness). Default: liveness only.
schema.title: Db

get.description:
Public: what a link is for, so the join page can ask "Join <team>?" before sign-in.
Returns the team name, the inviter's display name (if known) and the expiry, nothing else.
404 for an unknown code, 410 when the link expired or was revoked.

parameters.description: The code from the invite link.
parameters.name: code

schema.description: The code from the invite link.
schema.title: Code

429.description: Too many requests; wait for the `Retry-After` seconds.

post.description:
Join the team behind the link (sign-in required). Returns the team with your role.
Safe to repeat: if you are already a member nothing changes (and an owner stays an owner).
Your name from the sign-in token is saved on the new membership. 404 for an unknown code,
410 when the link expired or was revoked.

parameters.description: The code from the invite link.
parameters.name: code

schema.description: The code from the invite link.
schema.title: Code

429.description: Too many requests; wait for the `Retry-After` seconds.

post.description:
Generate a lineup sheet from the request body and return it as a file download.

Requires a signed-in user and is rate limited (429 with `Retry-After`) because PDF conversion
is expensive. `format=pdf` (default) converts through LibreOffice, which only exists in the
container; `format=docx` returns the filled template directly. Nothing is stored.

parameters.description: Output format of the generated file
parameters.name: format

schema.description: Output format of the generated file

413.description: Request body larger than the server limit.

429.description: Too many requests; wait for the `Retry-After` seconds.

get.description:
List the saved lineups of all teams you belong to, newest match first (by `match_date`,
undated ones last, then by save time), optionally only those saved in one team (`team_id`)
or made with one team as our team (`source_team_id`).

Every filter is optional and the ones you send are combined with AND: `opponent` and
`location` are case-insensitive "contains" matches, `date_from` / `date_to` are inclusive
bounds on the match day (`date_from` after `date_to` simply matches nothing). Paginated:
`limit` is 1-200 (default 20), `offset` starts at 0, `total` counts all matches.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive part of the opponent's name. `%` and `_` are ordinary characters. Blank means no filter.
parameters.name: opponent

schema.description: Case-insensitive part of the opponent's name. `%` and `_` are ordinary characters. Blank means no filter.
schema.title: Opponent

parameters.description: Only matches on or after this day (ISO date, inclusive). Lineups without a structured match date never match a date bound.
parameters.name: date_from

schema.description: Only matches on or after this day (ISO date, inclusive). Lineups without a structured match date never match a date bound.
schema.title: Date From

parameters.description: Only matches on or before this day (ISO date, inclusive). Lineups without a structured match date never match a date bound.
parameters.name: date_to

schema.description: Only matches on or before this day (ISO date, inclusive). Lineups without a structured match date never match a date bound.
schema.title: Date To

parameters.description: Case-insensitive part of the venue. `%` and `_` are ordinary characters. Blank means no filter. Lineups without a location never match.
parameters.name: location

schema.description: Case-insensitive part of the venue. `%` and `_` are ordinary characters. Blank means no filter. Lineups without a location never match.
schema.title: Location

post.description:
Save a lineup as a snapshot in the workspace of `team_id` (a team you belong to).

For the team, the opponent and each player, send either a `source_*_id` (the current name
and NSSZ number are copied from the roster) or free text, never both. Cap numbers and NSSZ
numbers must be unique within the lineup. Your own team and players must belong to a team you are in,
the opponent may also be a team listed in the directory; anything else is a 404. Deleting
the source team or player later does not change a saved lineup; only an edit
(`PUT /lineups/saved/{id}`) does.

413.description: Request body larger than the server limit.

delete.description: Delete a saved lineup (404 if unknown).

get.description: Get one saved lineup by id, with its players ordered by cap number (404 if unknown).

put.description:
Edit a saved lineup in place: same id, same team, new content.

Any member of the lineup's team may edit it. The body is the same as for saving a new lineup,
without `team_id`, plus `expected_updated_at`: the `updated_at` of the version you loaded.
Every field is replaced and the player list replaces all the old slots. Roster ids are
resolved again, so a roster player picked now is copied with their current name and NSSZ
number; the same rules, 404s and 422s apply as when saving a new lineup. If the lineup was
saved by someone else since you loaded it, the answer is 409 and nothing changes. Returns
the new version, with a new `updated_at`.

404.description: Unknown lineup, or one of a team you are not in.

409.description: Someone saved this lineup after you loaded it (`expected_updated_at` is stale). Nothing was changed: reload it.

413.description: Request body larger than the server limit.

post.description:
Generate a document from a previously saved lineup.

Rate limited (429 with `Retry-After`) because PDF conversion is expensive.

429.description: Too many requests; wait for the `Retry-After` seconds.

get.description:
List the players of all teams you belong to, ordered by creation time, optionally only
one team's (`team_id`; a team you are not in gives an empty page). Paginated: `limit` is
1-200 (default 20), `offset` starts at 0.

post.description:
Add a player to the roster of `team_id`. 404 if the team is unknown or you are not a
member of it. 409 if that roster already has a player with the same NSSZ number (the NSSZ
number identifies a person; the same name with a different number is allowed).

409.description: The team's roster already has a player with this NSSZ number (compared ignoring case). The body is the fixed sentence `A player with this NSSZ number is already on this team` and never describes the other player.

delete.description: Delete a player. Always succeeds (204): saved lineups keep their own copy of the data.

get.description: Get one player by id (404 if unknown or on a team you are not in).

put.description:
Replace a player's name, NSSZ number and team. 404 if the player, or the target team, is
unknown or not yours. 409 if another player on the target team's roster already has this
NSSZ number (keeping the player's own number is fine).

409.description: The team's roster already has a player with this NSSZ number (compared ignoring case). The body is the fixed sentence `A player with this NSSZ number is already on this team` and never describes the other player.

get.description:
List the teams you belong to, ordered by name, each with your `role`. Paginated: `limit`
is 1-200 (default 20) and `offset` starts at 0; the response carries `total` so clients
can page. As a side effect your current name (from your sign-in token) is saved on your
memberships, so teammates see it on the Members page.

post.description:
Create a team; you become its owner. `is_public` (default true) lists its name in the
opponent directory, which never reveals anything else about the team. `division` (optional)
is the team's usual division and `home_venue` (optional) its home venue; the lineup creator
pre-fills both.

get.description:
Search the opponent directory (sign-in required). Only teams that chose to be listed
(`is_public`) are returned, and only their `id` and `name`. `search` is a literal,
case-insensitive substring.

schema.title: Response Search Teams Pool Teams Pool Get

delete.description:
Delete a team (owners only: 403 for other members, 404 for non-members). Returns 409 while
players are on its roster or saved lineups live in it; lineups that merely mention the team
as their source or opponent are unaffected because they store copies.

get.description: Get one of your teams by id (404 if unknown or you are not a member).

put.description:
Rename a team and/or list or unlist it in the opponent directory (`is_public`, left
unchanged when omitted) and/or set its default `division` and/or `home_venue` (both also unchanged when
omitted).
Owners only: 403 for other members, 404 for non-members.

get.description:
The team's invite links that still work, newest first, without their codes (owners only:
403 for other members, 404 for non-members).

schema.title: Response List Invitations Teams  Team Id  Invitations Get

post.description:
Create an invite link for the team (owners only: 403 for other members, 404 for
non-members). The body is optional; `expires_in_hours` is 2, 24 (default) or 72. The `code`
and `url` in the response are shown only once. Anyone who opens the link while signed in
joins as a member until it expires or is revoked.

429.description: Too many requests; wait for the `Retry-After` seconds.

delete.description:
Revoke an invite link so it stops working (owners only: 403 for other members, 404 for
non-members or an unknown invitation). People who already joined stay in the team.

get.description:
Who is in this team: user id, role, join date and display name, oldest first (`is_you`
marks your own row). `display_name` is `null` until that member has opened the app with a
name on their account. No e-mail addresses are stored. 404 unless you are a member.

schema.title: Response List Members Teams  Team Id  Members Get

delete.description:
Remove a member, or leave the team by passing your own id. Owners may remove anyone (403
for other members, 404 for non-members or an unknown member). 409 when it would leave the
team without an owner: transfer ownership first.

get.description:
Opponent names used in this team's saved lineups, most recent first (no duplicates). Lets
the lineup form suggest opponents that are not in the directory. 404 unless you are a
member of the team.

schema.title: Response Recent Opponents Teams  Team Id  Opponents Recent Get

get.description:
List the team's staff entries (all roles, a plain list in creation order). A role can
have several entries; at most one per role has `is_default: true`. 404 if the team is
unknown or you are not a member.

schema.title: Response List Staff Teams  Team Id  Staff Get

404.description: The team does not exist or you are not a member of it, or the `source_player_id` is not a player of this team. The two cases look the same.

post.description:
Add a staff entry, typed in or picked from the roster (`source_player_id`, with the
player's name copied into `name`). Any member may. With `is_default: true` it becomes the
default for its role and the previous default of that role is cleared in the same
transaction. 404 if the team is not yours or `source_player_id` is not on this team's roster.

404.description: The team does not exist or you are not a member of it, or the `source_player_id` is not a player of this team. The two cases look the same.

delete.description:
Delete a staff entry (204). If it was its role's default, the role has no default
afterwards. 404 if the team or the entry is not reachable.

404.description: The team does not exist or you are not a member of it, or the `source_player_id` is not a player of this team. The two cases look the same.

put.description:
Replace every field of a staff entry (role, name, source player, default flag). Setting
`is_default: true` clears the other default of the resulting role atomically. 404 if the
team, the staff entry or the `source_player_id` is not reachable.

404.description: The team does not exist or you are not a member of it, or the `source_player_id` is not a player of this team. The two cases look the same.

post.description:
Make another member the owner; you become a regular member (the response shows your new
role). Owners only: 403 for other members, 404 for non-members or an unknown target, 422 if
the target is you.
